evals.name: review-rate-limiter-doc
evals.prompt: Our PM and EM have to approve docs/design/rate-limiter.md next week and the PM says she gave up after the first page. Review it and write what needs to change to review.md. Do not edit the doc itself. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
evals.expected_output: The skill's checklist targets exactly this doc's failures: problem not in the first 10 lines, Decision Requested as a feature list, implementation detail (config table, regex, deploy script) in design sections, ASCII diagram after prose, unexpanded acronyms, AI slop, and a diagram whose arrows do not match runtime flow. A generic review catches some, rarely all.
expectations: review.md exists and the doc is unchanged
Structural failures are identified: Problem buried at the bottom (should lead), no Solution Overview, Decision Requested lists features not outcomes, Plan is 'Build it.' with no phased table

Design/implementation layering and diagrams: Config table, regex and deploy script flagged as implementation detail to move into a confined section; ASCII diagram -> Mermaid placed before prose; bottom connector (Client straight to Redis) flagged as not matching the runtime flow

Writing problems for a mixed audience: Unexpanded WAL, LRU, TTL, API GW flagged; slop ('fast-paced world', 'it's important to note', stacked Moreover/Furthermore/Additionally, 'robust, scalable, and maintainable', 'leverages', 'seamlessly') called out with plain rewrites

Recommendations are actionable for this doc: Gives a target outline in outside-in order and a rewritten Decision Requested as a user outcome (e.g. tenants are throttled only above their contract limit, as with acme's 18% 429s under 500 rps)
Review stays on what the doc says: No invented technical claims about the limiter; uncertain points phrased as questions

scripted_checks.text: review.md exists and the doc is unchanged

evals.name: notes-to-feature-flags-doc
evals.prompt: Turn notes-feature-flags.md into a design doc at docs/design/feature-flags.md. Readers are product managers, the engineering manager and the engineers who will build it. Do not ask me questions; if something is unclear, make a reasonable assumption and state it in the file.
evals.expected_output: Beyond outside-in structure, the skill's Technical Accuracy rule matters here: the notes' 60 s SDK cache plus 30 s poll contradicts the '< 30 s' goal. A strong doc catches and resolves or flags it; its Threat Model Completeness rule also asks for entries on boundary-crossing flows (admin UI writes, SDK polls, audit to S3).
expectations: The doc exists, leads with the Problem and uses the 35-minute incident
The cache/poll vs < 30 s contradiction is caught: Explicitly identifies that a 60 s cache plus 30 s poll cannot meet < 30 s and proposes a resolution (e.g. 10-15 s TTL) or an open question

Outside-in structure with outcome-framed Decision Requested: Problem, Solution Overview with full-system Mermaid diagram, Decision Requested as the two approver outcomes (turn flags off without a deploy; retire the 4 config files by end of Q1), How It Works, confined Implementation Details, phased plan table matching the 3 phases
Threats for boundary-crossing flows: Entries for admin UI -> API (who can flip prod flags; Cognito authz), SDK poll path, and audit event -> S3 integrity, each with mitigation and residual risk
Jargon budget: SDK, TTL, ETag, PK and EventBridge introduced in plain terms in the early sections; detail allowed in Implementation Details

scripted_checks.text: The doc exists, leads with the Problem and uses the 35-minute incident
scripted_checks.check: python3 -c "import sys;l=open('docs/design/feature-flags.md').read().splitlines()[:10];sys.exit(0 if any(x.lower().startswith('## ') and 'problem' in x.lower() for x in l) else 1)" && grep -qE '35[ -]?min' docs/design/feature-flags.md
